title: Large Network limit for Latent Variable Process Models with Endogeneously Evolving Interactions among Multiple Types
summary: Motivated by the opinion and social dynamics literature, we rigorously study dynamically co-evolving latent space network models, where agent opinions evolve based on a latent state space model influenced by and influencing an underlying dynamically evolving graph determining their interactions. In contrast to earlier work, see [18], agents are allowed to be heterogeneous, i.e., of different types, and their dynamic evolution can capture behaviors like attraction and repulsion between and within groups.
